fix: Anthropic's post says the flaw "was patched upstream and backported to all maintained stable kernel branches." For distribution users, that fix arrives only in the vendor's kernel package. Debian, Oracle Linux, SUSE, and Amazon Linux have shipped fixed packages, at least for some of their kernels, but Ubuntu and RHEL have not. The fix makes the kernel wait until other CPUs finish reading the options before it frees them.
impact: The kernel's own CVE team rates it 9.8 out of 10 on the CVSS scale. Anthropic said on October 27 that its AI model wrote an exploit that uses the flaw to let a remote attacker with no credentials run commands as root on Linux servers with a multipath TCP listener. As of October 29, Ubuntu and RHEL have not released a fixed kernel.

impact: Cybersecurity firm GreyNoise said it has seen at least six successful exploitations of CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, colloquially known as “PHP2Shell.” The bugs were added to a U.S. government catalog of exploited vulnerabilities this week, and federal agencies were given until Thursday to install patches. In total, the researchers found 24 compromised firewalls that gave the hacker the ability to extract credentials and enumerate directories. They also obtained account credentials, private keys and network topology that includes IP addresses and more. “If any of these attacks worked, the compromise extends far beyond the perimeter firewalls into the organization's identity infrastructure,” they said.
